title: Learned postoperative records distinguish readmission in a colorectal-surgery cohort
summary: A bidirectional LSTM classifier was evaluated for readmission using records from 4,336 colorectal-surgery patients. The source reports internal discrimination with an 80:20 training/test split, using perioperative and postoperative information. The result is a retrospective clinical model evaluation, without established preoperative prediction, external validation or demonstrated benefit from changing surgical care.
ai_technology: Bidirectional LSTM classifier applied to reshaped clinical patient records
organization: University of Portsmouth; Portsmouth Hospitals University NHS Trust

evidence.tested: A prospectively maintained surgical database covered 4,336 operations during 2003–2019, including 321 readmissions. The paper compared multiple classifiers and describes an 80:20 split for readmission analysis. Its three-hidden-layer bidirectional LSTM reportedly achieved sensitivity 84.1% and specificity 90.9%. Predictor candidates included clinical, operative and postoperative variables; a reduced set retained length of stay and operative details.
evidence.unknown: Prospective database maintenance does not make model evaluation prospective. Feature selection and preprocessing isolation from testing are incompletely specified, and no external or temporal test was reported. Inclusion of postoperative variables prevents a preoperative risk claim; the permissible prediction time and all-variable leakage risks are not fully established. The reported 87.5% accuracy equals the mean of reported sensitivity and specificity, so it is not adopted as an authenticated population-weighted accuracy. Reshaping records for LSTM does not establish genuine longitudinal sequence learning. No causal effect of surgical approach or improvement in care was tested.
evidence.ai_role: The learned classifier combined clinical-record features to discriminate observed readmission labels, supplying the represented retrospective outcome-evaluation result. Conventional descriptive associations with surgical approaches are not attributed to AI discovery.

source_review.scope: Read actual primary clinical data provenance, preprocessing, feature selection, BI-LSTM architecture and split Methods, readmission Results and prediction-time limits. Source model code was not executed. Other length-of-stay/mortality models are not separately admitted or treated as causal clinical findings. Exact original article front DOI/title and fresh PubMed primary relationship metadata checked.
